paragraphs: The supplied text mentions him in Shabbat 83a, Beitzah 8b, and Avodah Zarah 9a. Hyman’s printed edition cites Arakhin 11b for Rami’s explanation following Abaye’s remarks.

notes.text: The saved William Davidson paragraph for Arakhin 19b discusses Abaye without confirming the attributed Rami son of Rav Yeiva resolution. The Arakhin citation remains open. The separate Shabbat 83a passage names Rami son of Rav Yeiva; no whole-folio or edition-wide absence is inferred from the saved Arakhin paragraph.

Hyman’s 1910 print (vol. III, p. 1103) cites Arakhin 11b. The supplied Wikisource text has 19b, the reference discussed in the preceding note. At 11b, Rami proposes that the question concerned the lamb brought with the omer, immediately after Abaye challenges the previous explanation. For Avodah Zarah, Hyman’s print gives the numeral 9, and the supplied text specifies 9a. The named passage consulted is Avodah Zarah 15a, where Rami explains the decree concerning testing an animal at the onset of Shabbat.
